steps.do: List the text color classes already used in table files.

K-003156.example: rg -o 'text-[a-z]+-[0-9]+' src lists text-gray-400, which is about 2.5:1 on white and fails 4.5:1. The plan replaces it with text-slate-600 on bg-white, which is about 7.6:1.

Write a Playwright spec that reads getComputedStyle for each .menu-item font-size and line-height.

Confirm the item font-size is 16px, which is 1rem at the default root size.

K-003173.check: The Playwright run prints '1 passed' or more, with 0 failed, and the reporter lists each assertion for five items.

A spec that runs against the Vite dev server may pick up unbuilt styles, so build first.

steps.do: Start the dev server on port 5173 in the background.
Run axe with the WCAG 2 AA tag set against the menu route.
Confirm normal menu item text reaches a 4.5:1 contrast ratio.
Confirm the menu heading at 1.25rem or larger reaches a 3:1 contrast ratio.

K-003174.example: Menu items use #1a1a1a on #ffffff, a ratio of 16.1:1, and the section heading uses #595959 on #ffffff, a ratio of 7.0:1. The axe run reports zero color-contrast violations for the menu.
K-003174.check: The axe output reports '0 violations' for the color-contrast rule, and the count of incomplete color-contrast checks is 0 for the menu selector.
traps: Axe cannot compute contrast over text on gradients or images, so it reports incomplete results, not passes.
A pass on the default theme says nothing about the dark theme, so run the check for each theme.
The 3:1 ratio applies only to text at 24px or 18.66px bold; body menu text needs 4.5:1.

steps.do: Confirm the dark theme block defines the menu color token.
Write a Playwright spec that sets data-theme to dark on the html element and reads the menu text color.
Run the theme spec in Chromium.
Confirm the dark menu text against its background reaches 4.5:1.

K-003175.example: The dark block sets --menu-text: #e6e6e6 and --menu-bg: #121212, a ratio of about 15.8:1. The spec sets document.documentElement.dataset.theme to 'dark' and asserts the computed color matches the token.
K-003175.check: The grep prints at least one match with 'data-theme' and 'dark', and the Playwright run reports '1 passed' with the computed color equal to rgb(230, 230, 230).
traps: Setting the theme attribute on the menu element instead of html can make a spec pass while the page itself stays light.
Computed colors come back as rgb() strings, so comparing against the hex token value fails.
A dark override that only changes text color can leave the active item background unchanged, so measure the item background too.

steps.do: Confirm the min-height token for menu items is set to 2.75rem.
Write a Playwright spec that reads each menu item boundingBox height and width.
Run the target-size spec in Chromium with mobile viewport settings.
Confirm every menu item height and width is at least 44px.

K-003176.example: The token file sets --menu-item-min-height: 2.75rem, which resolves to 44px at a 16px root size. The spec asserts that boundingBox().height is at least 44 for all six menu items.
K-003176.check: The grep prints the token line with 2.75rem, and the Playwright run reports '1 passed' with every measured height at 44 or greater.
traps: Padding can make a box look large while the text line box is smaller, so measure the element, not the text.
A 2.75rem token only gives 44px at the default root size, so a user with a larger root font gets a bigger target, which is fine, but a smaller root breaks the target.
Inline list items with display: inline do not take the min-height, so check the computed display first.

steps.do: Confirm the menu font-size declarations use rem units, not px.
Write a Playwright spec that sets the html root font-size to 20px and reads the menu item font-size.

steps.do: Start the dev server on port 5173 in its own terminal.
Install the Chromium browser that Playwright uses.
Run the breakpoint spec that measures grid column counts at 375px and 768px.
Confirm the run reports every test passed with no failures.

K-003385.example: At 375px the list must compute grid-template-columns with 1 track, and at 768px it must compute 3 tracks. The spec reads getComputedStyle on the list element at each viewport width.
K-003385.check: The output ends with '3 passed' and the failure count is 0.
traps: Testing only at the default desktop viewport and assuming the mobile layout is correct.
Writing max-width variants when the code is mobile-first, where md: means min-width 768px.
Checking the class string in the source instead of the computed layout in the browser.

steps.do: Start the dev server on port 5173 in its own terminal.
Install the Chromium browser for Playwright.
Run the overflow spec at a 320x568 viewport that compares scrollWidth with clientWidth.
Confirm the single matching test passed.

K-003386.example: A list row with an unbroken 80-character string must wrap, so document.documentElement.scrollWidth stays at 320 and does not exceed clientWidth. Add break-words or min-w-0 to the row's flex child if it does not.
K-003386.check: The output shows '1 passed', and the spec asserts scrollWidth is less than or equal to clientWidth.
traps: Using a fixed width such as w-[600px] on a list row, which forces sideways scrolling on phones.
Forgetting min-w-0 on a flex child, so long text pushes the container wider than the screen.
Testing with short sample text that never triggers the overflow.
